Schools

PHS holds annual Consent Assembly

By Julia Stokes · October 7, 2026 · 2 min read

On Wednesday, September 30, Piedmont High School held its annual Consent Assembly for seniors and freshmen. The assembly, organized by acting teacher Kim Taylor, junior Stella Joseph, and senior Ben Ramakrishnan, involved current PHS students reading real stories from anonymous PHS graduates about their experiences involving sexual assault and consent.

“The purpose of the Consent Assembly is to bring awareness and educate people about how to stay safe and how to prevent these stories from happening again,” junior Ida Marshall said.

Marshall was one of 16 students who read stories. Although Marshall is enrolled in acting, students do not need to take acting to present in the assembly. A goal of the assembly is for people from across the school to be involved.

“I think it went well. All of the other story readers were really talented and I thought we made the stories sound really real. I heard stories about people being affected by it,” Marshall said.

PHS also has a lunch club, Piedmont for Consent (P4C), that focuses on spreading awareness about consent. According to P4C co-president junior Sophia Puckett, the club’s goal is to make sure everyone feels comfortable about consent and their personal boundaries.

Puckett said that club events this year include giving presentations about what consent is at elementary schools in Piedmont, along with partnering with an elective class at Piedmont Middle School.

“The middle school has a new class that’s going to help us lead presentations for the elementary school. It’s called LEAD,” Puckett said. “It’s an elective class, and it focuses on consent next semester.”

P4C co-president junior Lucy Shoop said that they are working on a middle school assembly as well.

“We’re working on a script that the middle schoolers are going to use in the new elective. Basically, we’re going to help them teach,” Shoop said.

The Consent Assembly happened to coincide with the reopening of a 2024 sexual assault case at Cornell University, which sparked conversations across the PHS campus. Puckett said that Piedmont for Consent held an open conversation at lunch for students to share their thoughts about the case.

“I think with the Cornell case, a lot of the stories and conversations can be triggering for a lot of people, and we want to make sure people have a place they can come if they need something,” Puckett said.

Although Piedmont for Consent is not directly affiliated with the Consent Assembly, Puckett said that their goals very much align.

“The assembly is a great way that we are getting the message of consent culture out to Piedmont and other Bay Area schools,” said Puckett.

The Consent Assembly takes place once a year, and Marshall said she hopes to continue her involvement.

“I really enjoyed doing it. I thought it was a really meaningful and valuable experience, and I hope I’m able to do it next year,” Marshall said. “I think bringing awareness to this stuff is not talked about enough and that’s why it’s really important.”

Julia Stokes is a junior at Piedmont High School and a student writer intern for the Piedmont Post.
